newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco to purchase two Spanish ships at $35 mln.
newsitem.headline: Morocco to purchase two Spanish ships at $35 mln.

text.p: Morocco will purchase two ships for merchandise transportation to be built by the Spanish firm Union Naval de Levante at a cost of $35 million, an official of the fisheries ministry said on Tuesday.
The two ships, acquired by the state-run Compagnie Marocaine de Navigation (COMANAV), are expected to be delivered by end-1997, the official said.
COMANAV, which covers 50 percent of Morocco's maritime transportation, has a capital of 224.5 million dirhams ($26.1 million) and employs a staff of 1,700.
Established in 1946 in Casablanca, the firm has eight offices located on the Mediterranean and Atlantic coastlines.
